rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = reader stalls on a referent that never resolves under the sequential read. Walked all 6 chunks: chunk0 L3 'the M5/M6 loop... its own creation' and 'the same loop you just ran' are the module-arc opener carve-out — this file's own module include (spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md L34-38) places it directly after 'Map the gaps, read your stack' (the exercise), matching the maintainer block's own Delivery note (L80: 'after the exercise and before the Human close'). chunk2 L17 'the M5 move'/'those three modules' and L23/L27/L29 'the reference artefact' each carry disambiguating context in the same sentence. L25 'The closing lecture ended with a three-phrase benediction' names its subject in the same breath (the quoted phrase follows immediately) rather than pointing at a prior slide by position. chunk3 L39-41 'the loop', 'the banned word', 'the flattering end-state', 'chat-shaped' are all reused from earlier slides in the same file (chunk1/chunk2) per the rule's own explicit non-violation. chunk5 L53 'the M5 packaged session' is the same opener/closer carve-out as chunk0. Closest call: L59 'the move I am asking you to run' — resolves via chunk2 L17's 'run the M5 move on its own work', an earlier slide of the same file, so it stays inside the reuse carve-out rather than being a fresh unnamed referent.

Harm = a callback the reader can't locate without knowing another file's position. Two candidates in body: L25 'The closing lecture ended with a three-phrase benediction: "You know how to test... You know how to learn... You know how to encode."' and L27 'The closer's Ramp paragraph attributed a framing... "the harness was the bottleneck, not the model."' Both name the source by its content, unpacked in the same sentence, matching the rule's own passing pattern (name-plus-claim, not name-plus-position). No bare 'the opening lecture said' / 'as covered earlier' construction anywhere in body.

Harm = a chunk that reads as blank/wait-state when projected alone. All 6 chunks carry a developed unit that closes on its own frame: chunk1 (L9-13) closes 'Those numbers are the story' (L13); chunk3 closes 'A rule in context is not a rule in the output. Taste closes the gap.' (L41); chunk4 closes 'The model is good. It is still not 100% deterministic.' (L49). None is a bare context-dependent bullet or a pure wait-state.

Harm = a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Checked all 5 `##` headers against their bodies: 'The numbers' (L9) -> the tally paragraph; 'Things that went sideways' (L15) -> the six-item failure catalogue; 'The generalisation' (L31) -> the three one-line universal claims plus thesis; 'Then I compounded the session' (L43) -> the second-loop fix (rules moved into skills); 'What the loop is for' (L51) -> states the loop's rationale and closes the memo. Each is a true summary of its chunk; none contradicted by its own content.

Per sub-item, mechanical grep restricted to lines 1-64: 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' -> `grep -niE '\\bNot [A-Za-z].*\\. Not '` returns 0 hits (L5 'Not the pedagogy of it. The actual session.' is a single 'Not', not the banned two-Not-then-Z triple). Anaphora/epistrophe triples -> two chains found: L39 'The loop caught what the subagents missed. I caught what the loop missed. You will catch what I missed.' and L59 'I fixed what I caught. The loop caught what I missed. A senior-persona sim caught what the loop missed.' Both satisfy the rule's own exception: the third leg introduces a new concrete agent (the reader; the senior-persona sim) rather than repeating hollow escalation. Self-grading superlatives -> `grep -niE 'most (useful|important|valuable)|one of the (best|most)'` returns 0 hits (maintainer block L114 confirms the prior superlative was already cut 2026-08-30). Number+own-retraction -> the tally numbers (L11: 'Twenty-odd', 'Five', 'Four', 'Ten') are stated flatly with no hedge/retraction language following. Abstraction-noun stacks -> none found; L21 'post-training preferring warmth over directness' is a labelled owned inference per the backing block (L113), not an abstraction-stack. Verb triplets with an empty leg -> none found.
